key_insight: Continual learning for deepfake detection can worsen demographic unfairness over time, so preserving accuracy alone is not enough.
engineering_relevance: For deployed AI security systems, model-update strategies must be judged on both robustness and fairness because continual adaptation can shift error burden unevenly across groups.
method: Evaluated detectors on a chronological sequence of 11 real-world deepfake generation methods
Compared continual learning families: rehearsal, prompts, and regularization
evidence_signal: The study monitored fairness metrics over time while progressively training deepfake detectors on 11 sequential generator methods to reveal accuracy–fairness tradeoffs.
watch_item: Fairness gains were scarce and inequitable forgetting was not explained by underrepresentation alone, so dataset balance by itself may not prevent demographic harm.
paper_title: Time to Fake It: Continual Machine Learning Intensifies Unfairness in Deepfake Detection
